GA-139Brandingfor Jefsev's review

Mountains along the bottom

Gizai's own wireframe landscape as a band along the bottom of the window, from the left edge to the right edge, under the sidebar and the main column: more visible than what Omarchy lets through the window now, and never in the way of text or controls. Three strengths to pick from, on the board, the chat and the Editor, in dark and light.

Every screen is drawn with the app's own stylesheets (src/styles), so it looks as the app will; the band is band.css with its tokens in band-tokens.css (from new-tokens.json). Each screen shows dark, then light; the switches show one theme or one strength. The proposal is Medium: the band reads at a glance, and all three text colours keep 4.5:1 over it. Built by node design/branding/gen-bottom-band.mjs.

1. The artwork

Our own land, drawn by gen-bottom-band.mjs from seed 139: the same lines every time it runs, and no wallpaper or photo in it. A flat valley runs into the distance between ridged mountains, seen through a perspective camera, as a mesh of four-sided cells. The lines a nearer slope hides are taken out (a floating horizon, front to back), so the file holds only the lines you see; far lines fade, and the top of the picture fades so the peaks melt into the page above.

Seed 139mulberry32 and gradient noise: no randomness from outside the file
  • Sharp at every width. It is vector and has no tiles: one picture, centred under the window's middle and cut at the sides (preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMax slice"), so there is no seam to see. Its lines keep 1px at any size (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke).
  • Peaks on both sides at every width. The valley floor is 300px wide at the bottom edge, so even an 800px window shows the slopes rising on both sides of it; a wider window shows more ranges, smaller and fainter toward the sides.
  • A short window makes the band lower (§5.4): the picture scales down with it and shows more of its width.
  • One file for both themes. The lines are currentColor: the band's colour comes from band-line, so light needs no file of its own.

2. Three strengths on three screens

Gizai's first window size, 1440 × 900, where the band is 126px high. Subtle: About as much as Omarchy's see-through shows now: there when you look for it. Medium: Clearly there, never loud: the lines read at a glance, the glow tints the bottom edge. Strong: The bright strip of Jefsev's screenshot: the band is the first thing you see at the bottom. The switch at the top shows one strength.

The board

  • The canvas is see-through: the band shows under the sidebar, between the columns and below the cards. Cards stay solid, so their text never has the band behind it, and a live card's working strip keeps its teal on the card's own surface.
  • A long column's last cards stand in the band, and so does Review's “Show 2 more of 8” (text-2 on no surface of its own).
  • Under the sidebar the band runs behind Company's Usage, Team, Users and Settings (text-2, icons text-3). The sidebar's colour stays: it moves under the band.

The chat, with its composer at the bottom

  • The composer's strip is see-through and its box stays solid: the text, the hints (text-3), Runs on and Send never have the band behind them. The band shows beside the box and under it.
  • The threads column is see-through like the sidebar: its last rows (their times are text-3) and Archive stand in the band.
  • The messages stop at the composer's top border, so a message scrolls off before it reaches the band's strong part.

The Editor, with its status bar

  • The file tree is see-through like the sidebar: its last rows stand in the band (an ignored folder's name is text-3).
  • The code, its tabs, the status bar and the terminal panel stay solid: the band never runs behind code, where every character counts. So in the Editor the band shows under the sidebar and the tree, and the code column stands in front of it, its status bar on the bottom edge as now.

3. Text over the band

WCAG 2 contrast of the text colours over the band, where the band is strongest: its bottom edge, with the glow at full strength over the canvas (bg, or side under the sidebar, the threads and the tree), and a line at full strength over that. Each cell gives between the lines · on a line; under 4.5:1 is marked (under 3:1 for the focus ring, which is a control's outline, not text). Text sits higher than the edge almost everywhere (the sidebar's last row starts 12px up, where the glow is a tenth weaker), so these are the worst case.

  • Subtle and medium keep all three text colours at 4.5:1 or more between the lines, and text and text-2 at 4.5:1 even on a line; text-3 keeps 3:1 there. A line is 1px wide: where one crosses a letter, that pixel has the second number and the rest of the letter the first.
  • Strong keeps text and text-2 at 4.5:1 between the lines and text on a line; text-3 drops to 3.74–4.23:1 at the bottom edge, and a line crossing text-2 drops to 2.36–3.14:1. That is the price of the bright strip: picking it means the faint text near the bottom (thread times, an ignored file's name) reads less well there.
  • Controls keep their own surfaces (buttons, inputs, the composer box), so the band changes no control's contrast. The focus ring (focus), drawn around a row or a button that stands in the band, keeps 4.32:1 or more between the lines in every strength; where it crosses a line it can drop to 2.21:1 for that pixel in strong.
  • gen-bottom-band.mjs checks these numbers before it writes anything, and stops when a strength breaks its rule.

4. Colours: the band isn't a status

Teal means an agent at work and magenta “needs you” (design/README.md, Colour carries meaning). Jefsev's wallpaper is teal, so the band takes a cooler, quieter blue: one hue, 228° in OKLCH, between teal (live, 187°) and the accent's blue (266°), with less chroma than either and at a low alpha. It never pulses or moves: only the live pulse moves on its own.

5. How to build it

For the frontend card that builds the strength Jefsev picks. Nothing in the app changes in this card. The CSS is in band.css, which this page uses as it is; the tokens are in new-tokens.json.

5.1 Where the layer sits

One element, the window's lowest layer: the first child of .app, fixed along the window's bottom edge at z-index: -1, in the page's own stacking context. Everything in the window is above it; the canvases are see-through, so it shows between what is on them. No element gets a new stacking context, so menus portaled to the body, drawers, the palette, toasts and the close question keep the order they have now.

<html data-band="on">                       html's bg is the canvas; body's own background goes
  <div class="app">                           as now: no z-index, no isolation
    <div class="band" aria-hidden="true">     position: fixed; z-index: -1; the window's width, along its bottom
      <svg …>mountains.svg's lines</svg>       currentColor: band-line, on a glow of band-glow
    </div>
    <aside class="side">…</aside>             see-through: its colour on .side::before, z-index: -2
    <main class="main">…</main>               see-through: html's bg is its colour
  </div>
</html>
  • Inline, not an image. Band.tsx puts the SVG's markup in the page (Vite's ?raw import of mountains.svg), not an <img> or a CSS background: inline, the lines take currentColor, so one file serves both themes and every strength, and no mask image has to load.
  • The layers, bottom up: html's bg; the side-coloured columns' ::before (z-index -2); the band (-1), its glow and then its lines; then everything else in the window, in its usual order.
  • The glow is a gradient on the band itself: transparent at its top to band-glow at the bottom edge. The SVG fades its own top (a mask in the file) and its far lines.
  • Nothing else needs a z-index. Nothing in the app has a negative one now. Keep .app, .main, .chat and .ed without a stacking context (no z-index, opacity, transform or filter on them): one there would keep a column's ::before and the band apart.

5.3 Never in the way

  • pointer-events: none and user-select: none: clicks, drags, the wheel and selections go to what is above it. A card dragged to the bottom, or text selected down to the last line, works as now.
  • aria-hidden="true" on the element: screen readers skip it. It has no title, no role and takes no focus.
  • It never moves: no animation, so nothing for prefers-reduced-motion to stop. Only the live pulse moves on its own.
  • It takes no space: turning it on or off moves nothing.
  • It goes with the system's high contrast (prefers-contrast: more), in forced colours (Windows' contrast themes) and on paper.

5.4 Its height, and short windows

  • height: clamp(var(--size-band-min), 14vh, var(--size-band)): 128px in a window 915px high or more, 14% of the height below that, at least 80px. 1080 high: 128px. 900 (Gizai's first size): 126px. 768: 108px. 600 (Gizai's smallest): 84px.
  • The picture scales with the band's height and is cut at the sides, so a lower band shows the same mountains smaller, and more of them (§1).
  • Under 560px of window height the band goes: Gizai's own minimum is 600, but a tiling window manager can make the window shorter, and there the content needs the room more than the band.

5.5 The switch: Settings → Appearance

  • A new section at the end of Appearance, Background, with one checkbox: Show mountains along the bottom, on by default. Its hint: “Under the sidebar and the page, in the theme's colours. Off gives the plain background back.” As everything on this tab, a change shows at once, without Save settings, and is kept on this computer.
  • src/lib/appearance.ts gets band: boolean (default true), kept as gizai-band, and puts data-band="on" on <html> while it is on, before the first paint, as it does data-density. Reset to defaults turns it on again. App.tsx renders the band only while it is on.
  • No key for it: t and d stay the only Appearance keys.
Dark

5.6 For the frontend card

  • Tokens: from new-tokens.json, band-line, band-glow and the pair of the strength Jefsev picked to color.tokens after scrim, and size-band and size-band-min to size.tokens after size-statusbar; then node scripts/tokens-css.ts.
  • The artwork: mountains.svg to src/assets/, as it is (run the generator again to change it, then copy it again).
  • The CSS: band.css to src/styles/band.css, imported after appearance.css in main.tsx; the page-only .win[data-band] can go.
  • The component: Band.tsx, the element of §5.1, rendered as .app's first child while the setting is on; the setting as in §5.5.
  • Check by eye in both themes: the board with a long column, a chat, the Editor with the tree open, Settings, a task page with its properties, and a drawer open over the band.

band.css

/* The band (GA-139): Gizai's mountains along the bottom of the window, under the sidebar and the main column, behind
   everything in them. The frontend card moves this into src/styles (band-tokens.css shows the tokens until they are in
   design/tokens.json). In the app, <html> has data-band="on" while Settings → Appearance → Mountains is on, and the
   band is .app's first child; on the design page each frame (.win) carries data-band with its strength.

   The layers, from the bottom up, all in the page's own stacking context (the root), so no element gets a new one and
   menus, drawers, the palette and toasts keep the order they have now:
     1. the canvas: html's bg, and side under the side-coloured columns, on their ::before (z-index -2);
     2. the band (z-index -1): its glow, then its lines;
     3. everything else: the canvases are see-through, so the band shows between rows and cards; what holds content keeps
        its own background (cards, panels, inputs, the composer box, code, the status bar, menus, drawers). */

/* The layer: fixed along the window's bottom edge, the window's width. The lines are currentColor (band-line) on a glow
   that rises from band-glow at the bottom edge to nothing at the band's top. It takes no clicks, no focus and no text
   selection, and screen readers skip it (aria-hidden on the element). */
.band { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: -1; height: clamp(var(--size-band-min), 14vh, var(--size-band));
  overflow: hidden; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; color: var(--band-line); background: linear-gradient(transparent, var(--band-glow)); }
/* The artwork keeps its height and is cut at the sides (xMidYMax slice): its middle under the window's middle, its lines
   1px at every width (non-scaling-stroke). The file's own color attribute is only for opening it on its own: the band's
   colour wins. */
.band > svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; color: inherit; }

/* body's own background would cover a layer under it: html's, the same bg, is the canvas */
[data-band] body { background: none; }

/* Gizai's smallest window is 900 × 600, where the band is 84px; a tiling window manager can make it shorter, and there the
   band goes. It goes too with the system's high contrast, in forced colours and on paper. */
@media (max-height: 559px), (prefers-contrast: more), (forced-colors: active), print { .app > .band { display: none; } }

/* ---------- see-through: the canvases near the bottom ---------- */
/* The sidebar, the chat's threads and the Editor's tree: their colour moves to a ::before under the band */
[data-band] .side, [data-band] .chat-threads, [data-band] .ed-side { position: relative; background: none; }
[data-band] .side::before, [data-band] .chat-threads::before, [data-band] .ed-side::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -2;
  background: var(--side); pointer-events: none; }
/* The main column, the chat's composer strip (the box in it stays solid) and the properties panel: html's bg is theirs */
[data-band] .main, [data-band] .chat-composer, [data-band] .props { background: none; }

/* Everything else keeps its background and so stays solid over the band: cards and panels, inputs and buttons, the composer
   box and its banners, the Editor's code, tabs, status bar and terminal panel, the Terminal page, the Changes view, sticky
   table heads, menus, popovers, the palette, drawers and toasts. A row's hover and selected fill is solid too.
   A stacking context between .app and these columns (a z-index, opacity, transform or filter on .app, .main, .chat or
   .ed) would keep their ::before and the band apart: keep them without one. */

6. The website's hero (GA-52)

The same land, seen closer up: mountains-hero.svg comes from the same seed, the same terrain and the same camera, 3.5 times nearer and with a finer mesh: 3840 × 448 at 1:1, 42.7 kB. It sits along the bottom of the hero, in the band's colours at strong (the website has only a headline above it), with the headline and buttons in its sky. The text and the menu stand in for GA-52's.

  • As in the app it is inline SVG, cut at the sides (xMidYMax slice), its lines 1px at every size: on a wide screen more ranges show, on a narrow one the valley and its nearest peaks.
  • The glow is a gradient on the hero's band, from transparent at a fifth of its height to band-glow at the bottom.
  • The website can take the tokens' values as they are; it has no live agents, but keeping the band's blue keeps the website and the app one family.
